text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Although Gary Ablett has one year left to run on his contract, Geelong coach Gary Ayres has refused to guarantee the ageing AFL star's future after the Cats' 60-point loss to North Melbourne in the elimination final yesterday. Page 25.

After winning his fourth major triathlon title in the U.S. yesterday, Australian Greg Welch said the only goal he had left was the gold medal at the Sydney Olympics. Welch won the men's long-distance world championship in Indiana, ahead of Belgium's Luc Va Lierde and Britain's Spencer Smith in 3h47m5s. Page 26.

After importing two new Americans to their line-up following the Olympic break, the Perth Wildcats have lost four of their past seven games, including losses to Canberra (101-94) and North Melbourne (100-97) on the weekend. Injuries to Scott Fisher and Aron Trahair have compounded the problems of Perth who now have to fight for a top-four position in the National Basketball League playoffs. Page 26.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Karen Dalton came off the bench on Saturday night to propel the Sydney Flames to a 57-54 victory over reigning Women's National Basketball League champions the Adelaide Lightning. The Flames will host their second grand final in four years, against the wnner of next weekend's preliminary final. Page 24.

Although Randwick are favourites to win their eighth first-grade rugby union premiership in 10 seasons, they finished fourth on the premiership ladder after a final round which saw Easts defeat Warringah 30-22 and Eastwood beat Canberra 40-29 at Manuka Oval. Page 24.

Although many tipped a Manly-Brisbane rugby league grand final, Brisbane's 21-16 loss to Norths on Saturday means they will have to face Manly for a place in the final if they can beat Cronulla this weekend. Injured Brisbane props Glenn Lazarus and Andre Gee are uncertain starters for the clash with the Sharks. Page 25.
THE AGE

West Coast Eagles coach Mick Malthouse has accused Australian Football League officials of not being able to decide whether the AFL competition is national or just an expanded Victorian contest after Essendon won the right to host Saturday's semi-final aainst West Coast, despite losing to Brisbane last Friday. Page 2.

The Brisbane Lions have announced the signing of five former Fitzroy players, Brad Boyd, Jarrod Molloy, Chris Johnson, Scott Bamford and Nick Carter. The newly merged AFL club is expected to pick 10 Fitzroy players, but it is still unclear whether Matthew Primus will be selected after he said he would refuse to move to Queensland to play for the team. Page 3.

With three laps to go, touring car ace Craig Lowndes snatched victory from Glenn Seton's Ford yesterday, ending a three-year winning streak for the Ford team in the Sandown 500 endurance race. Lowndes and co-driver Greg Murphy finished first in a Commodore, with fellow Commodore drivers Peter Brock and Tomas Mezera taking third position. Page 16.
HERALD SUN
The Australia cricket side was thrashed by 50 runs in the final of the Singer Cup against Sri Lanka on Saturday, in a game which saw Steve Waugh cautioned for sledging Romesh Kaluwitharana. Page 82.

Once his National Basketball League season is over, Melbourne Tigers centre Mark Bradtke will sign a one-year contract with the Philadelphia 76ers for the minimum NBA wage of US$247,500. Bradtke will also earn a further US$70,000 from NBA merchandise revenue. Page 84.

Scoring just four points in the first half, the Perth Breakers' Gina Stevens exploded in the second half to take Perth to a 75-58 victory over Bulleen in yesterday's Women's National Basketball League semi-final. Page 84.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Filante owners Geoff and Beryl White confirmed yesterday that Australia's new weight-for-age star could be a starter in the A$5 million Japan Cup. Two invitations will be open to Australasian horses and after two wins in two starts this season, Filante is a sure chance to get the nod. Page 36.

South Australian golfer Anne-Marie Knight shot 66 yesterday to join Laura Davies on seven-under 209 in the third round of the European Open at Hanbury Manor, England. After shooting a tour record-equalling 63 on Saturday, Davies shot only 76 to drop to fifth. Page 38.

The Parramatta Eagles have won a place in the soccer semi-finals after defeating UTS Olympic 2-1 at Melita Stadium. Marconi and Sydney United have also booked semi-finals tickets after victories against Sutherland and Highfield Wolves. Page 39.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
